feature: An arrow tip lands on the edge it is pointing at
summary: Arrows, lines and boxes now magnetize to the borders the app has already found in the picture, the same way a measuring caliper does. Aim near an edge and the tip lands on it instead of a couple of pixels short, with the same yellow guide saying which edge it caught.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Open any screenshot. Nothing to turn on.

try.do: Open a screenshot with buttons or cards in it.
Press A for the Arrow tool and wait a second for the picture to be read.
Drag an arrow from empty space towards the left edge of a button, stopping a few pixels short of it.
Watch for the yellow line while the button is still down: it says which edge the tip has taken.
Let go, then press Escape to skip the caption. Zoom to 400% and look at the tip.
Aim a second arrow diagonally into a button's corner: both guides light and the tip lands on the corner.
Draw a third arrow at the same spot with Command held: the tip stays exactly under the pointer.
Press V, click the first arrow, and drag its tip handle: it magnetizes the same way.

evaluate: When you aim at a border, does the tip land where you meant it to on the first try?
Does the yellow line, drawn right across the picture, help or is it too loud for a mark that is only pointing at something?
An arrow drawn flat takes only the border ahead of it and keeps the height you chose. Is that what you expect, or should it also settle onto a nearby horizontal line?
Is Command the key you reach for to refuse the magnet, or do you expect that to be free by default with a key to turn it on?
Boxes snap too: drag a rectangle loosely round a button and it comes out hugging it. Useful, or in the way?
rough: The magnet reads the box the app detected, not the painted shape. On a button with a rounded corner, a tip that lands on the bounding edge next to the corner sits a hair off the paint. That reads correctly at the middle of an edge, which is where an arrow usually points.

Shift refuses the magnet as well as Command. It is not a second escape hatch by design: a Shift drag pins the arrow to 45 degrees around its other end, so the angle owns where the point lands and a magnet could only fight it.

Snapping does not offer element centres, unlike the Measure tool, which has a Snap picker for it. The picker is not reachable from the Arrow tool, so an arrow's behaviour would have changed under a control you could not see. Edges only for now.

The task asked to reuse the caliper's call as it stands. Two parts of it are deliberately not reused: the caliper's axis gate reads the direction the hand is travelling, and an arrow reads the direction the ARROW points instead, which is steadier; and the lines other measurements put down do not pull an arrow, only the picture's own edges do.

The first run showed the magnet defeating itself. A line caught mid-sweep used to ride along for the rest of the drag and park the tip a dozen points short of the aim. Fixed, and every drag in the walk still reports zero guides going back on themselves, so no flicker was traded for it.
